passage:
An old well stood in the center of a village. People no longer used it because every home had tap water.
When the village planned to cover the well, older residents objected. They said the well had been the place where people met, exchanged news, and helped each other during dry years.
The village repaired the stone wall around it and added a sign telling its story. The well remained closed for safety, but it was not erased.
A well is not only a hole for water. In many places, it was once a social center.
The village kept the well to remember a time when water had to be carried and community was built one bucket at a time.
